questions.text: The Yingzao Fashi, a 12th-century construction manual, documented standardized modules for which aspects of Chinese architecture?

options.text: Garden design principles and water channel engineering, focusing on aesthetic harmony and irrigation efficiency
Column and beam interlock, roof pitch, bracket size, and tile patterns following proportional rules

Feng shui orientation and cardinal alignment procedures, which were believed to influence prosperity and health

rationale.a: Garden design and hydraulic engineering are not mentioned as subjects of the Yingzao Fashi.
rationale.c: While glazed tiles are used symbolically, the manual's primary focus is structural and proportional systems.
rationale.d: Feng shui orientation is a planning principle, not documented construction specifications in a technical manual.
rationale.correct: Columns, beams, roof pitch, bracket size, and tile patterns follow strict proportional rules documented in the Yingzao Fashi, enabling rapid scalable construction.

questions.text: A wooden bracket system using interlocking blocks and arms to support roof overhangs without nails, enabling large interior volumes and seismic flexibility, is called ___.

options.text: Feng shui module, often used in traditional Chinese architecture for symbolic purposes
Dougong bracket system
Glazed tile veneer, typically applied for aesthetic enhancement of exterior surfaces
Siheyuan partition, a feature of courtyard houses that provides privacy and separation

rationale.a: Feng shui is a cosmological orientation principle, not a structural system.
rationale.c: Glazed tiles are ceramic roof coverings, not bracket systems.
rationale.d: Siheyuan is a residential courtyard typology, not a bracket system.
rationale.correct: Dougong is explicitly defined as a modular wooden bracket system using interlocking blocks and arms to transfer roof loads to columns without nails, enabling large overhanging eaves and seismic flexibility.
rationale.takeaway: Dougong is explicitly defined as a modular wooden bracket system using interlocking blocks and arms to transfer roof loads to columns without nails, enabling large overhanging eaves and seismic flexibility.

questions.text: Which imperial palace, constructed by Emperor Yongle of the Ming Dynasty from 1406–1420 in Beijing, features a 960-meter north-south central axis, yellow glazed tiles, and dougong-supported pavilions?

options.text: Temple of Heaven, known for its circular mound altar and triple-gabled roof, used for annual ceremonies of prayer to Heaven for good harvests
Summer Palace (Yuanmingyuan), a vast ensemble of lakes, gardens, and palaces in Beijing, known for its harmonious integration of natural scenery and architecture
Forbidden City (Palace Museum)
Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, a magnificent triple-gabled circular building, built on three levels of marble stone base

rationale.a: Temple of Heaven is a sacred ritual precinct, not the imperial residence; it features a circular, not linear, axial design.
rationale.b: Summer Palace (Yuanmingyuan) was built later (1707–1860 by Kangxi/Qianlong, Qing Dynasty), not by Ming Dynasty Yongle.
rationale.d: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is one component of Temple of Heaven, not the entire imperial palace.
rationale.correct: The Forbidden City is explicitly identified as the Ming Dynasty imperial palace built 1406–1420 by Emperor Yongle in Beijing, featuring a 960m north-south axis, yellow glazed tiles, 9 main halls, and dougong construction.
rationale.takeaway: The Forbidden City is explicitly identified as the Ming Dynasty imperial palace built 1406–1420 by Emperor Yongle in Beijing, featuring a 960m north-south axis, yellow glazed tiles, 9 main halls, and dougong construction.

rationale.c: The structures differ fundamentally in function and symbolic purpose, not merely material.
rationale.d: This reverses actual functions: Temple of Heaven is a sacred precinct; Forbidden City is the imperial residential and administrative center.

rationale.correct: Against confusing dougong with simple post-and-beam construction, specifying that dougong is a unique modular interlocking system without nails, restricted to sophisticated Chinese, Korean, and Japanese structures.
